quest.title: Treehouse Theater: Candlelit Shadows Dancing
quest.description: Go look for the last missing part!
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Really!? You'd do that? Oh, but that's too much, I can't...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No, really. It's alright, we want to do everything we can for the domain.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Yes, and to be completely fair, I'm the one who caused this terrible mess in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? What happened? Did Paimon miss something?

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hello, you two. Lessig was just telling us what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Perhaps you should allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Ahem, I'm afraid it was I who caused all this trouble in the domain.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes, it was Lessig...

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: To be precise, I saw a most exquisite water orb at the entrance of the domain. It reminded me of an astrolabe my grandfather gave me when I was seven years old...

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: I was curious if it could rotate, so I reached out and touched it.

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Little did I know that it was the core of this entire domain. Ahem, what I mean to say is... I knew something was wrong as soon as the whole place started flipping...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: It's not just your fault, I failed in my responsibilities as the caretaker here. *sigh* I knew I should have put the core somewhere more secure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean the big ball of water at the entrance?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yes, that's the one. Anyway, after giving it some thought, Lessig has offered to perform some more repairs and maintenance to help support the domain.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But we were concerned he wouldn't be able to handle it all alone, so Eula and I will also stay here to lend him a hand.

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: But don't be mistaken, I'm not doing this out of the kindness of my heart like Collei. My job is purely to monitor and ensure that Lessig doesn't cause any more trouble here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, sure...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't think anyone's buying that anymore, Eula. Though I do remember that Amber mentioned we should just nod and agree when you act like this...

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Ahem...!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, right! Uh, you better not slack off today, Lessig!

dialogues.speaker: Lessig
dialogues.text: Ah, no! I'll get right to work!

dialogues.speaker: Eula
dialogues.text: Hmph... Either way, Lessig is going to be in charge of making lunch for everyone today.

choices.text: That'll give him a chance to redeem himself.

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: Yes, I'll do my best. No need to worry!

response.speaker: Eula
response.text: What was that?

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: Oh, I mean... thanks everyone for giving me a chance to redeem myself. I can already feel new strength kindled inside me! Ah no, maybe that's just the heat of the oven!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Very good, but you should conserve your strength. Many parts of the domain are still in disrepair, so we have a lot to investigate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems Idyia has a little more pep in her step after finding others to help do the work.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Now that you three are situated, we can focus on what the rest of us will be doing today!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: I'll go gather the others. We should get ready to leave as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And there she goes... At least she seems to be happy.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Maybe this is how it feels to be in charge.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After waiting for a while, you head to the location of the final component together with Klee, Kaeya, and Kokomi, whom Idyia called over.

response.speaker: Lessig
response.text: Hmm? Ah, yes... I'll try, but I'm not sure if my skills will prove satisfactory...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: The director doesn't get out much, he's almost always cooped up in his tree house making props or writing scripts...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: But I'm trying to remember now... where is that tree house of his?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Huh? You don't remember?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Hey, don't forget... I'm just the Mascot, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I believe it's that way.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Though he might prefer to be alone, given he often has to move stage props, I suspect that he lives near the theater.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: And having a view of the entire stage would be useful when imagining a production's actual stage flow.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: So, if I were him, I'd probably pick a treehouse over there.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: But, how do you know which direction the theater is in?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Oh, simple. The overall layout and decorations look more exciting in that direction.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Oh, good point! Why didn't I think of that...?
Where did that blasted automation mechanism go...? The male actors' standees are here, but where are the female ones...
Hmm? Who's that... Idyia?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Yes, Zosimos. 'Tis I, Idyia! ...How's that for a dramatic entrance?

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: This is a surprise. I was sure you'd be—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Curled up in a fetal position crying to yourself"?

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Wow, what a fascinating little creature... Did you just read my mind?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The name's Paimon. And no, Paimon's no mind-reader... Just call it an educated guess.

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Haha, it seems everyone shares a similar opinion about you, Idyia.

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: I knew from the start that a managerial role wasn't for me... But I've found my true calling now. As a mascot.

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: "Mascot"? Is that a new role? I don't remember casting you for that...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: Okay, enough about me. I'm just here to introduce you to some new friends of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Idyia introduces everyone to Zosimos and explains all that has happened...

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: ...And that's why we came to see you! Well? Do you have the component that fell out of the Central Hub?

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: I do, however...

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: I'm afraid the incident has caused many malfunctions with the stage mechanisms, and I can no longer put on any performances...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so you're holding the component ransom till we help you fix the mechanisms, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Idyia
dialogues.text: No. Till we fix the stage, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I'd have thought he wants us to make some more props, no? Given that some of the standees are missing?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Or maybe the component is broken, and we need to fix it!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: You're all forgetting that the majority of his work involves writing scripts. I'll wager that he wants us to edit them.

choices.text: Who started this guessing game, anyway?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: ...What has gotten into you all? What sort of person do you take me for!? The component is safe and sound — I can give it to you now if you like.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Although I was hoping that maybe you might be willing to... help rescue my show.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: You're a big group, I have lots of roles to fill... It would really speed up the casting.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: A show? Hee-hee, that sounds fun!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: I wanna help! Can we, can we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So far so good...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Also... Truth be told, I've hit a bit of a roadblock in my script and was just thinking about how to move the story forward... And then you all showed up.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Suddenly, I got my muse back! I don't know how to explain it, but... something about seeing all of you finally helped me figure out how to continue my script!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Huh? You mean that story you've been stuck on forever? Are you serious? You really think you can finish it now?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Yes! Really! Just give me a little time, and I'll write it all up! In the meantime, I'll leave things to you, Idyia.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Idyia's mouth is wide open as she watches Zosimos rush to the corner, panting up a storm as he whips out his pen and starts penning his script...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, and he's off to write the script...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: *sigh* Zosimos has always wanted to write an epic story about a thief and a mage. Apparently, he got the idea from some rumors that were swirling around, but he only got as far as writing the intro before writers' block set in...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Why don't you all take some time for yourselves while I see what I can do? We'll reconvene after the director finishes his script.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Some time later, Zosimos flies in brandishing a stack of scripts to hand out to everyone.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone is astonished that he finished an entire script in such a short time.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: A director, my friends, is a storyteller. And the key ingredient to every good story is inspiration! The moment I laid eyes on General Sangonomiya, inspiration hit me for a brand new character.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: The heroine was the missing piece of the puzzle. The rest of the story flowed naturally from there, and now it's finished! So please, take a look through your scripts, and we will tell this story together!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone reads their scripts as Zosimos gives pointers about how it will play out on the stage...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Well? Is everything clear?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Uh, Director Zosimos? How do you pronounce this word?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Let me see... Ah, that's "sojourn," it means to stay for a while. This is a very cute moment, so make sure that comes through in the performance.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Oh wait, there's another word I don't know here...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: It's okay, Klee. We can go through your lines together a few more times after this meeting's over.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: That would be most appreciated, Kaeya. I had a feeling about you, actually. You seem to know a thing or two about character acting. Tell me, have you acted before?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Haha, you're too kind. It's all in the script, really. It just rolls off the tongue.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Oh, you think so? Well, you definitely have a knack for it. I've actually been looking out for someone with your talent.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: If I make it as a big time director, then I can see us working together for the long term! Be sure to stay in touch, okay? You and I are gonna go places...

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: What can I say? Sounds good to me.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Great, fantastic... Now then, please go through your scripts one more time — but don't just read the words. Remember my notes, and really let the character inhabit you. I need to have a look at the stage, so I'll leave you to it.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: If you need me for anything, I'll be in the big theater right in the center of this area.

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Where did it go? I put it right here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Zosimos! Whatcha up to?

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two.

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Please, come here. Feast your eyes on this stage! I designed it myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So directors have to design the stage, too?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Haha, I'm no ordinary director. I take a more holistic approach... Directing, script writing, stage design... I do it all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a lot of work. Idyia wouldn't be able to handle that kind of job.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Idyia has her work cut out for her too, you know. She's my one and only member of the audience... Though she often criticizes my shows...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She has the gall to sit there and criticize you?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Well, she just says what she thinks. "You don't know how to write," or "this is getting ridiculous"... I think it's because I use preprints in a way that she feels goes against what they're intended for.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: But even though she's my harshest critic, she's also been my biggest supporter in a lot of ways. I guess you could say she's like my agent.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: I'm very grateful to her. I've always dreamed of being a director, but I never had the chance until I came here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what did you do before you came here?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Like I said... I dreamed, heh.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: From a young age, every time I came home after a show, I'd go over the story again and again in my mind. Growing up, my biggest aspiration was to be a director.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Unfortunately, I couldn't offer much beyond my practical skills... so I ended up spending most of my time as a prop designer, and doing a bit of set design on the side.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Don't get me wrong, I do love building the set, but... nothing satisfies me more than putting on my very own show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder you only wrote "director" on the sign.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Haha, exactly... You're not doing a great job of convincing me that you're not a mind-reader.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: By the way, could I ask for your help with something? I'm having trouble finding the master script, and I'll need it shortly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The one you only just finished writing? You lost it already?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Yeah... After I handed everyone their copies, I held onto my master copy while I was checking on everything around the theater... I must've dropped it somewhere.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: But, uh... I still have some things to do to get the stage ready. Would you two mind having a look for me?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: If it's not here, then it might be in the attic. These are the only two places I've been since I finished writing it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No problem. We'll find it.

dialogues.speaker: Hydro Eidolon
dialogues.text: Gurgle!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this is a lot of scripts...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the Water Droplet has been managing them for the director...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, most of them look like works in progress...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay. Well, we're looking for a master script, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, then it should be the one that's finished! Okay, so let's look for the thickest one, and then check the ending...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the only script that fits the bill, plus it looks pretty new... This must be the master script.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go give it to Director Zosimos!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zosimos, we got your script!

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Ah, thank you! That's a huge help. *sigh* ...I'm running out of time here, there's no way I'll be able to fix everything up perfectly. We may just have to wing it.

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Anyway, the stage is secondary — the performance is what really matters. Things can always go wrong on stage, but as long as the show goes on... it should be fine...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't sound very confident in what you're saying...

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: It's true! I realize now that a show is the art of the unknown!

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: Even if you have the same actors performing on the same stage, the performance will be slightly different every time. Those subtle differences are what make each performance special!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: #Ugh... Okay, one last request. {NICKNAME}, you can enter the preprints, yes?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: The truth is that my sets are composed entirely of preprints... First, I use materials to make the objects, then I take those objects and turn them into the preprint.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Now, of course, preprints are really meant for making objects to furnish the domain. So using objects to create preprints is, strictly speaking, the reverse of what this is intended for.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: But Idyia said that if this is what I really want to do, she's not going to stand in my way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so that's what you meant earlier... Okay, well, what do you need us to do?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: #I'd like {NICKNAME} to go into the preprints set and help move props around during the performance...

choices.text: So I'm part of the backstage crew now...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: The reason is, um... Heh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You want to watch the show.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhh, Paimon gets it now. If you're busy directing, moving the props, and operating all the mechanisms, you never get the chance to watch the show...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: ...Yes. I know that I'm no master-playwright, but still...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Even if it really is a half-baked script, with shoddy writing, and moments of sheer ridiculousness... I'd still like to see it for myself, just once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hard to turn a guy down after a speech like that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're more than happy to help!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Thank you! Genuinely, I'm so grateful! I'll go and inform the others, then — as soon as you're ready, the show can begin!

choices.text: You have a point, but I'm not completely convinced.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And we're done! Seems the show went pretty well.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} Honorary Knight!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Didn't I do great? I felt like I really was the fiery mage!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, great costume, Klee!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As soon as Paimon saw your shadow, she thought straight away: What a cute hat!

choices.text: It's the role you were born to play!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Klee loves it! Thanks, Mr. Zosimos!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Wait, no! I mean, uh... Mr. Director!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Mr. Director...?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Wow! No one's ever called me that before! Thank you, my dear little mage, thank you so much! I'm so happy!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Miss Idyia said that she tailored it a little bit so it would fit me, but you were the one who designed and made it. You're amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that is amazing! And it sounds like Idyia did a great job, too!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: It was nothing, really. Just one of those "Oh no, whatever shall I wear to the ball" moments... Sewing comes in handy at times like that.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Sewing is an art in its own right. You're more talented than you give yourself credit for, Idyia.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Really? Oh, uh... I—I'm just gonna go for a second... please, chat amongst yourselves...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She gets embarrassed so easily... She really can't handle being in the spotlight.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Idyia's a sensitive person, and doesn't have a whole lot of self-confidence... I hope all the excitement hasn't brought her to tears? Hmm, I'm a little worried...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Don't worry, I'll go make sure she's okay. I'll see you all later.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: So, what did you all think of the play? Any thoughts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Uh-oh, time to get serious! Now, are you sure you want to hear what we really think?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Oh, absolutely! I had the courage to ask, didn't I? So don't mince your words. Go ahead, speak your mind. I can take it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, since he's asking for it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, Paimon will go first! So the dialogue at the beginning was pretty good, but it ran out of steam as the story went on, Paimon could tell that you ran out of inspiration somewhere along the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The characters were honestly a little bit ridiculous. Paimon didn't get what you were trying to do — the moment anyone started to show any kind of substance, suddenly the scene was over!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Yes, all very good points, Paimon. I would add that in its attempt to pay tribute to the series "A Thousand Nights," all semblance of a coherent was sacrificed. Plus, I do have to penalize you for the issues with the props.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Miss Idyia? What are you doing back here?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Oh, you know... I return like the tide when people start discussing something important!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Especially when it has to do with criticizing my show!

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Mm-hmm! But there was one thing I liked about it... just one, mind you. The story had a good ending.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Idyia's even harsher than Paimon.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: ...You think so? I thought I was letting him off lightly.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Idyia, could I borrow you for a moment?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Oh, sure! Excuse me for a moment. Back to you, Paimon! Keep up the good criticism.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! In that case, Paimon did have one other complaint.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Let's hear it! Taking criticism on the chin is all part of being a director.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The ending was all wrong. The girl's motives were clear and simple the whole way through. It was kinda jarring when all she had to say was "I dunno."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And doesn't anyone else find it weird how her whole community was on the run... but she was only looking out for herself the whole time?

choices.text: So even the "good ending" wasn't so good.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: I'm fine. I'm not going to improve without feedback! I also learned a lot this time with the chance to be offstage. To be honest, it was a dream come true.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a great attitude! You don't seem upset at all by our comments.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: I wouldn't say I'm completely unaffected, but you're only speaking the truth. They're all very valid points.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, now that Paimon thinks about it, you did finish the script in a bit of a rush... Hmm, maybe we are being a little too hard on you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was quite ambitious.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Haha, that's perfectly fine. Nothing is as important to me as my work on the stage.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: We all use our imaginations when we're kids, right? I used to play with dolls and my own cardboard cutouts by the light of an oil lamp. The shadows would come to life and dance on the walls... I never got tired of it.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Fast forward to now, and in many ways I'm still that same little kid, lying on his bed making sound effects. And I get the same joy from running a show now as I did in my little bedroom theater.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: ...Of course, a director can accomplish nothing without a cast and crew, so on that note, I want you all to know that I am eternally grateful to each and every one of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't mention it! We had a blast!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Hahaha... Okay here, take this. Your component, as promised.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: It's the bottle from the show! The one that lit up when I blew into it!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: That's right. Can you guess the secret behind why it lights up?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Ummm... Oh, maybe there's an invisible fairy inside that opens its eyes when you blow into it!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Bingo! You guessed it.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: That should do the trick? Oh wait, this needs tightening up a little... Hold on, this will only take a second.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Hmm? Something interesting's going on over there...)

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: This outfit's more fashionable than I imagined...

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Excuse me, everyone, do you have a moment? Especially you, Zosimos. Idyia wants to do a little something for you — she says it'll be a dream come true.

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: A dream come true?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Yes. She said that as useless as she is, she wants to do something for you as the first person to have heard of your dream of being a director.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Her words, not mine. I have to disagree though — I have never thought of Idyia as a useless person.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: How is this suddenly about me...

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: If everybody is ready... then I'd like to invite tonight's male lead to take the stage! Ta-daa!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wooooow!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Cool! Kaeya's turned into the real dagger bandit!

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Um, how is me changing outfits supposed to make the director's day? It's just a prototype costume... Is he that easy to please?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Don't be silly! If I know our director, nothing will make him happier than to see his ideas brought to life by the right actor.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hahaha... Well, then I'm happy to oblige. Who am I to argue with the star of the show?

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Zosimos drew up countless designs and made a few prototypes before landing on this one. It just needed some tailoring to fit properly, so I made a few stitches here and there... I hope the result isn't a disappointment?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: ...It's perfect, Idyia, I... I'm...

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: I'm... *sobs* I'm so touched... Thank you all, you've made me happier than I ever thought I could be...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After seeing his performance for the first time, Zosimos cries tears of joy for a dream come true.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: How're you doing? Recovered?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: I'm good. Thank you again, Idyia.

response.speaker: Idyia
response.text: Oh please... Don't mention it. Well, now that we have the final component, it's time to say goodbye for now. Let's head to the core of the Veluriyam Mirage and get this place fixed up.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Can I keep wearing my costume?

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Please do, by all means. Both of you can keep your costumes, it seems only fair.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yay! Kaeya, keep wearing yours too, it looks amazing!

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I agree with our mage. I'm sure it's not every day you get to play such an unforgettable character.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Sure. I think I can be a bandit for a little longer.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Bye-bye, Mr. Director!

response.speaker: Zosimos
response.text: Take care, my dear friends!

dialogues.speaker: Zosimos
dialogues.text: The thicket board's mechanism should be functioning... Let's see, there's the lights... Oh, and the microphones...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wonder what the theaters are like here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go check it out while everyone's still getting ready!
